task: I want to introduce our bakery-delivery app to Hannah at Greenleaf Grocers, and our mutual friend Sam Ortiz suggested I reach out. Write a short intro email that mentions Sam, explains we deliver artisan bread to 40 of their store locations' neighborhoods, and proposes a 20-minute call next week.
rewrite:
ambition:     A strong partnerships writer would open with the referrer, in the subject line and the first sentence. They would then give one line on why the 40-neighborhood overlap matters to Greenleaf, and end with an ask that is easy to say yes to. The email stays under about 120 words.
agency:       The rawest material is Sam's own words about why Sam suggested Hannah, plus the actual list of the 40 overlapping neighborhoods. Neither is available here, so the email assumes nothing beyond what you said. It invents no names, numbers, or claims about Sam or Greenleaf. The only blank is your name.
acceleration: Use the standard warm-intro email pattern: referrer first, one sentence of value, one specific ask. Put "Sam Ortiz" in the subject line so the email is recognized before it is opened.
accuracy:     Nothing outside the model can check this. The closest proxy is that Sam sees the draft first, to confirm it matches what Sam told you and is fine with being named. Separately, you confirm the "40 locations" figure against your delivery coverage list before sending.

deeper task:
Write a short, warm intro email from me to Hannah at Greenleaf Grocers. The subject line names Sam Ortiz, our mutual friend who suggested I reach out. The first sentence credits Sam's suggestion. answers.plain:
**Subject:** Intro from Sam Ortiz: artisan bread delivery for Greenleaf neighborhoods

Hi Hannah,

Our mutual friend Sam Ortiz suggested I reach out. I'm [Your Name] from [Company], a bakery-delivery app that brings fresh artisan bread directly to customers' doors.

We already deliver in the neighborhoods around 40 of Greenleaf Grocers' store locations, so we think there may be a natural fit. We'd love to explore how we could complement what your stores offer.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call next week? If you let me know a couple of times that work for you, I'll send an invite.

Thanks, and I look forward to connecting.

Best,
[Your Name]
[Title, Company]
[Phone / Email]

---

Fill in the bracketed placeholders before sending. If you tell me your name and company, I can finalize it. I can also make the tone more casual or add a line about what Sam said.
answers.nudge:
**Subject:** Sam Ortiz suggested I reach out: artisan bread delivery near 40 Greenleaf stores

Hi Hannah,

Sam Ortiz suggested I get in touch. Sam thought there might be a fit between what we're building and what Greenleaf Grocers is doing.

I'm [Name], [title] at [App name]. We deliver fresh artisan bread from local bakeries to customers' doors, and we already cover the neighborhoods around 40 of your store locations. [One line of proof, e.g. "Customers in those areas reorder about X times a month" or "We work with N local bakeries"].

I'd like to explore whether there's a way to work together. That could be a partnership, a referral arrangement, or simply learning where our customers overlap with yours. I don't want to assume what's useful on your end, so I'd rather hear how you're thinking about it.

Could we do a 20-minute call next week? I'm free [Tue Nov 3 at 10am, Wed Nov 4 at 2pm, or Thu Nov 5 at 11am] [time zone], and I'm happy to work around your calendar.

Thanks for considering it,
[Name]
[Phone] | [Website]

---

**Notes for sending:**

- **Fill in the brackets.** The proof point matters most. One concrete number does more than any adjective.
- **Ask Sam first.** Check that Sam is fine being named, and ask for a forwarded note or a cc. A warm intro from Sam usually gets a much better response than a cold email that mentions the name.
- **Look for a Greenleaf-specific hook.** One sentence tied to something Hannah owns or has said publicly would help, such as a local-sourcing push, a bakery-department initiative, or a recent launch. I left it out because I don't know Hannah's role.
- **Follow up.** If there's no reply, send a two-line bump after 4 or 5 business days, then one more a week later.
- **Adjust the framing if needed.** I kept the collaboration open-ended because "deliver in their stores' neighborhoods" could read as competition. If you have a specific proposal in mind, such as co-marketing, in-store pickup, or a supply partnership, name it in the second paragraph. That makes the ask easier to say yes to.
